sources.title: Matam (région), Wikipédia
sources.says: Created by law 2002-02 of 15 February 2002 from the former Fleuve (Saint-Louis) region; departments per decree of 21 February 2002.

events.what: National Assembly adopts law 2008-14 raising Sédhiou, Kaffrine, Kédougou departments to regions; limits left to decree

sources.title: Loi n° 2008-14 modifiant la loi 72-02 (vie-publique.sn)
sources.says: Raises the departments of Sédhiou, Kaffrine and Kédougou to regions (14 regions), adopted 2008-02-01; the territorial extent, limits and capital of the regions are fixed by decree.

sources.title: Regions of Senegal (Statoids), 2008 entry
sources.says: Kaffrine, Kédougou and Sédhiou split from Kaolack, Tambacounda and Kolda; the law was passed 2008-02-01 and the decree took effect 2008-09-10; governors installed 2008-09-01 to 09-03.

events.what: Decree 2008-747 creates new departments and arrondissements, among them Guinguinéo

sources.title: Département de Guinguinéo, Wikipédia
sources.says: Created by decree 2008-747 of 10 July 2008; arrondissements Mbadakhoune and Nguélou (created 2008); part of Kaolack region.

events.what: Decree 2008-1025 fixes the 14 regions; Guinguinéo (from Fatick, with Mboss from Kaffrine department) in Kaolack

sources.title: Regions of Senegal (Statoids), 2008 entry
sources.says: Kaffrine, Kédougou and Sédhiou split from Kaolack, Tambacounda and Kolda; the law was passed 2008-02-01 and the decree took effect 2008-09-10; governors installed 2008-09-01 to 09-03.

sources.title: Kédougou (région), Wikipédia
sources.says: Created 2008 by partition of former Sénégal oriental (Tambacounda region); decree 2008-1025 of 10 September 2008 (JO 6446).

sources.title: Kaolack (région), Wikipédia
sources.says: Region created by the reform of 24 March 1984; in 2008 Kaffrine became a region and Guinguinéo was transferred to Kaolack from Fatick region.

sources.title: Communauté rurale de Mboss, Wikipédia
sources.says: Mboss was in Nguélou arrondissement, Guinguinéo department, Kaolack region; split in 2011 into Mboss commune and Dara Mboss rural community.

sources.title: Regions of Senegal (Statoids)
sources.says: Seven regions at independence (Cap Vert, Casamance, Diourbel, Fleuve, Sénégal Oriental, Sine-Saloum, Thiès); 1976-06-26 Louga split from Diourbel; 1984-03-24 Casamance and Sine-Saloum split, three renamings; 2002-02-21 Matam; 2008-09-10 Kaffrine, Kédougou, Sédhiou.

sources.title: Subdivisions du Sénégal, Wikipédia
sources.says: From 1960 to 1964 the administrative map had 7 regions: Cap-Vert, Casamance, Sine-Saloum, Fleuve, Sénégal oriental, Thiès, Diourbel; in 1964 circles became departments.

Guinguinéo department (2008) joined Mbadakhoune arrondissement and Ourour (Gossas department, Fatick region) with the Mboss rural community (Birkelane arrondissement of Kaffrine department, Kaolack region) inside one arrondissement, Nguélou; the pre-2008 Fatick/Kaolack line runs inside the geoBoundaries Nguélou atom. Pre-2008 Fatick = Fatick + Foundiougne + Gossas + Mbadakhoune + the non-Mboss part of Nguélou (+ Taïf until 2002); pre-2008 Kaolack = Kaolack + Nioro + the four Kaffrine departments + Mboss.
